ga-dnr-legal-pets.title: Georgia DNR: Guide to Legal Pets
ga-dnr-legal-pets.note: Corn Snake and Milksnake both appear by name on DNR's own prohibited-native-species list, with the page stating plainly that origin or morphology doesn't matter.

il-herps-act.title: Illinois Administrative Code, Title 17, Part 885 — Herptile Code
il-herps-act.note: Official Joint Committee on Administrative Rules text; §885.20 sets the 8-total/4-per-species cap on native herptiles and §885.80 sets the $50 Herpetoculture Permit that exempts a keeper from it.

mn-97a-401.title: Minnesota Statutes 2025, Section 97A.401
mn-97a-401.note: Subd. 8 states a pet snake, lizard, or salamander must come from a permitted breeder or have been possessed before August 1, 2021; hosted on the MN Revisor of Statutes' own site.

ne-163-nac-4-008.title: Nebraska Administrative Code, Title 163, Chapter 4, § 008 — Keeping Wildlife in Captivity
ne-163-nac-4-008.note: The Captive Wildlife Permit species list in §008.01B names only wild birds and wild mammals; reptiles never appear on it, which is the basis for treating common exotic reptiles as outside this permit system.

nj-7-25-4-5.title: N.J.A.C. 7:25-4.4 Exempted Species and 7:25-4.5 Additional Species
nj-7-25-4-5.note: Official NJDEP Fish & Wildlife exempted-species list; 4.5 requires a permit for any exotic reptile not named in 4.4's list, which covers Boa constrictor, garter snakes and ribbon snakes but not corn snake, milk snake, or rosy boa.

pa-exotic-wildlife-permit.title: 58 Pa. Code Chapter 147, Subchapter N — Exotic Wildlife Possession
pa-exotic-wildlife-permit.note: Official Pennsylvania Code text of the Game Commission's exotic-wildlife permit framework; no dedicated descriptive PGC web page could be confirmed, and the Commission has issued no new permits under this framework since January 1, 2014.

sc-act177.title: S.C. Code of Regulations, Chapter 123, Article 5 (§§ 123-150 through 123-153.4)
sc-act177.note: Official codified text implementing 2021 Act 177; §123-151.3 carves out captive-bred corn snakes under 20 inches and eastern milksnakes under 10 inches from the general native-reptile sale/possession ban.

tx-tpwd-nonindigenous.title: TPWD: Nonindigenous Snake Permits (Controlled Exotic Snake Permit)
tx-tpwd-nonindigenous.note: Official TPWD FAQ page; the controlled list covers only non-native venomous snakes plus five named large constrictor species, so corn snake, milk snake, and rosy boa fall outside the permit requirement.

pa-58-79-3.title: 58 Pa. Code § 79.3 — Season and Daily Possession Limits (Chapter 79, Reptiles and Amphibians)
pa-58-79-3.note: Official Pennsylvania Code text; the catch-all 'native species not listed' line sets a 1-per-day/1-in-possession limit, and companion §79.4 requires a permit for continued possession regardless of the animal's origin.

ut-r657-53-tables.title: Species Tables for Utah's Reptiles and Amphibians
ut-r657-53-tables.note: Official Utah DWR table under R657-53; lists Western milk snake (Lampropeltis gentilis) under 'Limited possession' at 2 daily/yearly and 4 total per species.

wi-nr-16-12.title: Wisconsin Admin. Code NR 16.12 — Amphibian and Reptile Regulations
wi-nr-16-12.note: Official Wisconsin State Legislature code text; caps take/possession of native, non-listed amphibians, lizards and snakes at 5 individuals per species, with NR 16.13 layering on the purchase restriction for native species.

az-co43-reptile-regs.title: Arizona Reptile and Amphibian Regulations 2026–2030 (Commission Order 43)
az-co43-reptile-regs.note: Official AZGFD regulations booklet effective Jan. 1, 2026; lists rosy boa (Lichanura roseofusca/trivirgata) with a take limit of 2 per year and 4 in possession under a valid hunting license.
